initial.reason: Exact same diagnosis; true diagnosis is a subtype description of POEMS syndrome.

relevant_findings.edema: 3+ pitting edema of the legs to the waist.
relevant_findings.strength: Decreased strength in the arms and legs.

family_social.social_history: The patient lived with his wife and children, rarely consumed alcohol, and did not smoke. He was a businessman and used leg braces and a walker to ambulate.

imaging_1.findings: Pachymeningeal enhancement along the calvaria and the falx cerebri, enhancement of the dura and multiple cranial nerves, and arachnoid granulation that narrowed the right transverse sinus.

lab_1.changes_over_time: Decreased to 29.0% six weeks before admission, increased to 34.1% on admission, and slightly increased to 34.6% four weeks after discharge.

lab_2.changes_over_time: Decreased to 10.0 g/dL six weeks before admission, increased to 11.8 g/dL on admission, and decreased to 11.5 g/dL four weeks after discharge.

other_1.changes_over_time: EMG and nerve-conduction studies showed decreased sensory responses, absent sural-nerve responses, prolonged F-wave latencies, and more prominent denervation in the tibialis anterior and medial gastrocnemius muscles compared to the previous study.
other_1.findings: Prolonged F responses in both feet, normal motor and sensory responses in the distal segments of the arms, and no motor responses in the intrinsic foot muscles.

stored_observations.present_illness: The patient had been well until approximately 4 years earlier when paresthesias of both feet, weakness of the lower legs, and bilateral foot drop developed gradually. Symptoms worsened over time, with increasing weakness in the legs and arms and the development of intermittent stabbing pain in the lower legs.
stored_observations.prior_history: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) diagnosed 4 years earlier. The patient had a history of knee surgery and erectile dysfunction for the past year. He also had dyslipidemia and hypercholesterolemia controlled by diet.

exam_1.changes_over_time: At age 24, mild spastic left hemiparesis was observed and evolved into severe bilateral ptosis and nystagmus by age 26. There was no improvement in ptosis with edrophonium. Initial normal visual acuity and optic fundi were maintained with no optic nerve abnormalities.
exam_1.relevant_findings: At age 24, there was mild spastic left hemiparesis, brisk reflexes except for absent ankle jerks, both toes up-going on plantar stimulation. No rigidity, bradykinesia, or tremor was noted. Sensation was normal. At age 26, the patient had severe bilateral ptosis, prominent gaze-evoked nystagmus, and some extraocular motor paresis.

family_social.family_history: Family history includes maternal grandfather diagnosed with LHON and was blind, and a maternal great aunt who was also blind with a relative who experienced subacute blindness.
family_social.social_history: Attended special education classes; never employed; continued to live at home.

imaging_1.date: 7 days after the onset of deafness
imaging_1.findings: Bilateral gadolinium enhancement of the intracanalicular portions of the seventh and eighth nerve complexes, consistent with inflammatory neuritis.

other_1.changes_over_time: Hearing loss progressed to total deafness over two days.

stored_observations.present_illness: The patient developed abrupt onset of severe bilateral ptosis at age 26. Nystagmus and extraocular motor paresis were also noted. The ptosis did not improve with edrophonium. The patient had a history of developmental milestones until age 8, followed by gait, speech, and intellectual abnormalities.
stored_observations.prior_history: Undefined progressive multisystem neurodegenerative disorder; cognitive dysfunction since age 13; mild spastic gait and bilateral hyperreflexia; previous cognitive evaluations showed low IQ scores.

lab_1.findings: Increased total bilirubin 131.2 µmol/L, direct bilirubin 22.2 µmol/L, glutamyl transpeptidase 598 U/L, and alkaline phosphatase 324 U/L.

lab_2.findings: Alanine transaminase 61 U/L, aspartate aminotransferase 86 U/L, total bile acid 109 µmol/L, and phosphorus 3.22 mmol/L.

stored_observations.present_illness: Symptoms began after birth, with prenatal oligohydramnios discovered at 28+4 weeks of gestation. The infant experienced poor weight gain that was initially unresponsive to an amino acid formula at 1 month, and later improved on a high calorific formula from 4 to 6 months. However, deterioration in appetite and weight gain occurred again from 7 months. At 9 months, the infant weighed 7.4 kg and showed impaired motor development. By 1.5 years, weight was recorded at 8.2 kg, indicating failure to thrive.
stored_observations.prior_history: The infant suffered from chronic renal function damage since birth, characterized by elevated serum creatinine and stage 5 chronic kidney disease (CKD) at birth, improving to stage 3 from 9 months to 1.5 years.
